content.text: {"quote_faithful":"yes","verdict":"confirmed","evidence_kind":"invalid_inference","fatal":"yes","explanation":"The definition fixes v(B) using the decreasing ordering, whereas Lemma 4.1 and the proof of Theorem 4.2 establish only that some ordering has nested absolute difference g. Nested absolute difference is not order-invariant: for {8,5,2}, decreasing order gives 1, while the order (5,2,8) gives 5. Thus Theorem 4.2, as stated, does not follow from its proof, and the quoted strategy unjustifiably returns to decreasing order. The intended upper-bound construction is readily repaired by processing the elements in the ordering supplied by Lemma 4.1, since the cutting mechanism works for any specified order; however, that repair is not written, so the all-n upper bound is formally incomplete as written."}
